answer.evidence: With 576 inputs the default init range is about ±0.0417, which is ±80 in these integers, so values beyond about ±80 mark weights that moved during training. Those trained weights form only two kinds of pattern. (1) Centre-positive blob detectors: units 3, 8, 21, 24, 27 and 28 have broad positive regions over roughly rows 3–20 and cols 4–20. Their peaks are all central, e.g. 99 at r10c15 (unit 8), 99 at r15c13 (unit 27), 98 at r12c15 (unit 28), 99 at r15c10 (unit 24). (2) Centre-surround units: 2, 5, 14, 16, 18, 19, 25, 29 and 30 have strongly negative centres (e.g. -96 at r14c11 in unit 29, -90 at r13c13 in unit 2, -90 at r8c14 in unit 14) and diffusely positive borders on all sides. Unit 19 has a mildly positive top band (rows 0–6) and units 14, 25 and 30 have elevated means on rows 1 and 3. These are weaker than the central effects, and since the same units' borders are positive on all sides, they look like generic surround responses rather than a compact artifact. Units 0, 4, 10 and 22 stay within init range. Units 1, 6, 9, 11, 12, 13, 15, 17, 23, 26 and 31 are shifted uniformly negative with no localized structure. I found no small block of consistently large same-sign weights in any corner or edge patch, which is what a pasted marker, text or border artifact would produce. In layer 2, unit u1 (output weight +88) receives positive weights from all six centre units (71, 40, 73, 62, 76, 99) and negative weights from most surround units (e.g. -80 from unit 25, -56 from units 2 and 30). That wiring fits a nodule-size/density readout, not a spurious cue.
answer.main_feature: The model mainly measures how much bright, solid tissue fills the centre of the crop (nodule size and density) through centre-positive units feeding layer-2 unit u1 toward malignant. Centre-versus-surround contrast units modulate this, adding information about the nodule's margin and its surroundings.
